title: Unramified scheme morphisms are etale local on source and target
statement: Let $P$ be the property of a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] being unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Etale morphisms mean [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $P$ is etale local on source-and-target in the following explicit sense: (i) if $e:U\to X$ is etale and $f:X\to Y$ has $P$, then $fe$ has $P$; (ii) if $f:X\to Y$ has $P$ and $b:V\to Y$ is etale, then $X\times_YV\to V$ has $P$, where the fibre product is [def-pc-fibre-product]; (iii) for every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, $P(f)$ holds if and only if for every $x\in X$ there exist schemes $U,V$, etale maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, a point $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, and $h:U\to V$ satisfying $fa=bh$ and $P(h)$. The statement includes the empty scheme and imposes no quasi-compactness, separation, or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 04R3 (remark-list-local-source-target), item (9), with Tag 04QZ (definition-local-source-target); source locality is Tag 03YV (lemma-unramified-etale-local-source), target locality Tag 02VM (lemma-descending-property-unramified), combined by Tag 04R2 (lemma-etale-local-source-target).

proof.text: For (i), an etale map e is locally of finite type and formally unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Convert unramifiedness to these two properties by [def-weil-unramified-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified], compose using the Mathlib instances realizing [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-composition-cancellation], and recover the open-immersion diagonal by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified]. For (ii), apply the Mathlib base-change instances [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-base-change], then the same diagonal criterion. No hypothesis on the base-changing morphism is used.

For the forward implication of (iii), if $f$ is unramified, take $U=X$, $V=Y$, $a=1_X$, $b=1_Y$, $h=f$, and $u=x$. Identity maps are etale by the cited definitions: on affines their ring maps are flat and finitely presented with no generators or relations; their diagonals identify with the identity, which is an open immersion. Thus these are the required charts.

Conversely, assume the charts in (iii) exist at every $x$. Unramifiedness of $h$ includes local finite type by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] to the property locally of finite type and these exact squares $fa=bh$. Its pointwise locality clause gives that $f$ is locally of finite type. Moreover $b$ is unramified because it is etale, so [lem-sfb-scheme-unramified-composition-cancellation] gives that $g:=fa=bh:U\to Y$ is unramified for every chosen chart.

source.place: Tag 04R3 (remark-list-local-source-target), local finite type entry; Tag 03YV (lemma-unramified-etale-local-source), finite-type and composition inputs

proof.text: Fix $x$ and one chart point $u$ above it. Put $y=f(x)$, $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{U,u}$. Functoriality of stalk maps identifies the composite $R\to A\to B$ with the actual stalk map of $g=fa$; the equality $a(u)=x$ identifies its base ring with $R$. Since $g$ is unramified, [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-formally-unramified] makes it formally unramified, and [lem-sfb-formally-unramified-stalk-map] makes $R\to B$ formally unramified. Hence $\Omega_{B/R}=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero]. Also $a$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; [def-weil-flat-morphism] says its stalk map $A\to B$ is a flat local homomorphism, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] makes it faithfully flat.

source.place: Tag 03YV (lemma-unramified-etale-local-source), differential vanishing and faithful flatness argument; algebra.tex Tags 04E8, 00UO, 00HR

proof.text: The etale map a is smooth by the Mathlib Etale-to-Smooth instance (using [def-weil-etale-morphism]), so [lem-sfb-smooth-stalk-formally-smooth] makes A -> B formally smooth. The private ring helper proves [lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-differentials-injective] directly from Algebra.H1Cotangent.exact_δ_mapBaseChange: a kernel element comes from H1Cotangent A B, which is zero by formal smoothness. Since Omega(B/R) is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero], the injection makes B tensor_A Omega(A/R) zero. Apply the exact Mathlib orientation of [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective], TensorProduct.mk A B (KaehlerDifferential R A) 1, to inject Omega(A/R) into that zero tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No tensor-factor interchange is needed. Thus Omega(A/R) is zero and the same differentials criterion makes the actual stalk map R -> A formally unramified.

source.place: Tag 031K (lemma-ses-formally-smooth), applied to the stalk tower; descent.tex Tag 03YV (lemma-unramified-etale-local-source)

proof.text: The preceding argument applies at every $x\in X$. Hence [lem-trf-formally-unramified-from-all-stalks] gives formal unramifiedness of $f$. Combine it with local finite type from step 3 using [lem-weil-pbc-lft-formally-unramified-unramified]: the diagonal is an open immersion, so $f$ is unramified. If $X$ is empty, the stalk condition and the pointwise local-finite-type condition are both vacuous, and the same two cited criteria still apply. Thus no point, finite subcover, quasi-compactness, separation, or Noetherian hypothesis has been added.
